subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
description: Students perform arithmetic with numbers in scientific notation. They add, subtract, multiply, and divide numbers of the form $a \times 10^{n}$ (where $1 \le a < 10$ and $n$ is an integer), convert between standard form and scientific notation, and re-normalize results so the coefficient satisfies $1 \le a < 10$. They handle problems mixing decimal and scientific notation, compare magnitudes of very large and very small quantities, and choose units of appropriate size (e.g. nanometers vs. kilometers) for real-world measurements.
subSkills: Convert a number from standard (decimal) form to scientific notation $a \times 10^{n}$ with $1 \le a < 10$
Convert a number from scientific notation back to standard form
Multiply numbers in scientific notation: multiply coefficients, add exponents, then re-normalize
Divide numbers in scientific notation: divide coefficients, subtract exponents, then re-normalize
Add or subtract numbers in scientific notation by first matching the powers of 10
Re-normalize a result so the coefficient satisfies $1 \le a < 10$ (adjust the exponent)
Operate on mixed forms where one quantity is in decimal form and the other in scientific notation
Compare two quantities in scientific notation to decide how many times larger one is
Choose units of appropriate size for very large or very small measurements

problemArchetypes.name: Multiply in scientific notation
problemArchetypes.example: Compute $(3 \times 10^{4})(2 \times 10^{5})$. Multiply coefficients and add exponents: $6 \times 10^{9}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Divide in scientific notation
problemArchetypes.example: Compute $\dfrac{8 \times 10^{7}}{4 \times 10^{3}}$. Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: $2 \times 10^{4}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Multiply or divide requiring re-normalization
problemArchetypes.example: Compute $(6 \times 10^{4})(5 \times 10^{3})$. The coefficient $30$ is not in $[1,10)$, so rewrite $30 \times 10^{7} = 3 \times 10^{8}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Add or subtract with matching powers
problemArchetypes.example: Compute $(4.5 \times 10^{6}) + (3.2 \times 10^{6})$. Same exponent, so add coefficients: $7.7 \times 10^{6}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Add or subtract with different powers
Mixed decimal and scientific notation
problemArchetypes.example: A bacterium has length $2 \times 10^{-6}$ m. How long are $0.0003$ of them lined up? Compute $(3 \times 10^{-4})(2 \times 10^{-6}) = 6 \times 10^{-10}$ m.

problemArchetypes.name: Compare magnitudes (how many times larger)
problemArchetypes.example: The Sun's mass is about $2 \times 10^{30}$ kg and Earth's is about $6 \times 10^{24}$ kg. About how many times more massive is the Sun? $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{30}}{6 \times 10^{24}} \approx 3.3 \times 10^{5}$ times.

problemArchetypes.name: Choose an appropriate unit
problemArchetypes.example: A virus is $3 \times 10^{-8}$ m wide. Express this in nanometers ($1\text{ nm} = 10^{-9}$ m): $30$ nm, a more natural unit.

Easy.description: A single operation (one conversion, or one multiplication/division, or one addition/subtraction with matching powers) where the coefficient result is already in $[1,10)$ so no re-normalization is needed.
constraints: Exactly one operation or one conversion
Coefficients are simple values (single digit or one decimal place)
For multiply/divide the resulting coefficient stays in $[1,10)$ (e.g. $2 \times 3 = 6$, $8 \div 4 = 2$)
For add/subtract the two numbers share the same power of 10

Medium.description: One operation that forces re-normalization of the coefficient, or add/subtract requiring the powers to be matched first, including negative exponents.
constraints: Multiply/divide where the coefficient leaves $[1,10)$ and must be rewritten (e.g. $30 \times 10^{7} = 3 \times 10^{8}$ or $0.5 \times 10^{3} = 5 \times 10^{2}$)
Add/subtract where exponents differ and one term must be rewritten before combining
Coefficients may carry one or two decimal places

Hard.description: Multi-step word problems that mix decimal and scientific notation, chain two or more operations, compare magnitudes, or require choosing an appropriate unit, and always demand a properly normalized final answer.
constraints: Requires extracting quantities from a real-world context (astronomy, biology, computing, finance)
Two or more chained operations, or a comparison division followed by interpretation
Mixes a decimal-form quantity with a scientific-notation quantity
May require converting to or choosing a more appropriate unit
Final answer must be re-normalized to $1 \le a < 10$ and labeled with correct units

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student multiplies the exponents instead of adding them when multiplying
Student adds the exponents instead of subtracting them when dividing
Student forgets to re-normalize when the coefficient is $\ge 10$ or $< 1$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Leaves the answer as $30 \times 10^{7}$ instead of $3 \times 10^{8}$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student adds the coefficients without first matching the powers of 10
Student also adds (or subtracts) the exponents when adding or subtracting the numbers
Student miscounts decimal places or moves the point the wrong direction when converting
Student mishandles the sign of a negative exponent during multiply or divide
Student divides the larger coefficient by the smaller regardless of order in a comparison
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Inverts the comparison ratio, e.g. reports $3 \times 10^{-6}$ times instead of $3.3 \times 10^{5}$ times
